Re-derived from bytes: Psalm 105 is identity-numbered and untitled (45 WEB = 45 MT verses); every dual-cite in the row checks via ps_lib. FINDING TESTED AGAINST THE ROW: device_notes reads '(darkness, blood, frogs, insects, hail, locusts, and the death of the “firstborn”) covers 7 of the traditional plagues and omits the livestock-pestilence and boils material present in this psalm's own catalogue by their absence'. The catalogue's plague nouns from bytes: חֹ֭שֶׁךְ (oshb:Ps.105.28), לְדָ֑ם (oshb:Ps.105.29), צְפַרְדְּעִ֑ים (oshb:Ps.105.30), עָרֹ֑ב AND כִּ֝נִּ֗ים (oshb:Ps.105.31, two nouns under one verb), בָּרָ֑ד with אֵ֖שׁ לֶהָב֣וֹת (oshb:Ps.105.32), אַרְבֶּ֑ה AND וְ֝יֶ֗לֶק (oshb:Ps.105.34, again two nouns), בְּכ֣וֹר (oshb:Ps.105.36). The sibling row M8-Ps-341 counts oshb:Ps.105.31 as two nouns (arov, kinnim); this row collapses them into 'insects', and that collapse is what yields 7. On the row's own stated terms - exactly two omissions named against a set of ten - 7 plus 2 cannot close at ten, so the digit is false as written, and the trailing clause 'present in this psalm's own catalogue by their absence' is self-contradictory. The count OBJECT is also unnamed and out of scope: 'the traditional plagues' is an Exodus-scoped set the Ps-scoped staged tools cannot sweep (the section 11 OL-c28 class - scope explicitly or drop). ROW TESTED AGAINST THE FINDING: nothing load-bearing rests on the digit - device_notes itself calls it 'texture, not boundary authority', the row's front seam stands on the wayyiqtol-plus-new-subject וַיָּבֹ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מִצְרָ֑יִם (oshb:Ps.105.23, byte tier) and its rear seam on the third-plural-to-third-singular subject shift שָֽׂמוּ (oshb:Ps.105.27, Moses and Aaron) to שָׁ֣לַֽח (oshb:Ps.105.28, YHWH) with the general-to-itemized turn. SEVERITY: confirm at medium - a false digit not alone load-bearing; not low, because a digit that contradicts its own arithmetic is an evidence defect, not a register slip. REPAIR PROPOSAL validated adversarially and endorsed WITH QUALIFICATION: the auditor's replacement digit '8 distinct plague objects across 105:28-36' is itself count-object-dependent - at the noun level oshb:Ps.105.34 also carries two nouns (אַרְבֶּ֑ה, וְ֝יֶ֗לֶק), so a byte-scoped noun count is 9 plague nouns (10 if אֵ֖שׁ לֶהָב֣וֹת at oshb:Ps.105.32 is counted rather than read as the hail's accompaniment), while '8' is true only under the Exodus-traditional mapping (arov and kinnim as two plagues, arbeh and yeleq as one) - exactly the cross-book object the finding says the staged tools cannot verify. Any rewrite must name its object: either the byte-scoped noun count with its digit, or the traditional count with its cross-book scope disclosed as unverified here; the strike of the self-contradictory clause is endorsed as written. both_sides_assessed false: a count-object item concerning no seam (the digit touches neither web:Ps.105.22|web:Ps.105.23 nor web:Ps.105.27|web:Ps.105.28). Marks: pmarks_Ps.json kq = 1 note at oshb:Ps.105.28 (the pair sits verse-finally after the quoted opener שָׁ֣לַֽח; correctly disclosed, outside the span) and 1 at oshb:Ps.105.18 (outside the span); no Selah in Psalm 105 (word-bound sweep). span_change false, so span_ruling n/a. In this catalogue the ASYNDETIC perfects mark each new plague (105.28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 34) and the wayyiqtols carry consequences (105.33, 105.35) or the climactic strike (105.36): the shipped seam falls between two asyndetic plague openers - as much a list-item boundary as any in 105.28-32 - whereas the 'rival' at 105.32|105.33 would cut one plague from its own consequence line and is byte-WEAKER, not stronger. The shipped grouping also coincides with a byte-visible rhythm change the row never states: one verse per plague at 105.28-31, then two-verse plague units at 105.32-33 and 105.34-35, then the single-verse climax at 105.36. The formula at 105.31 and 105.34 opens the two swarm plagues, three verses apart with the hail between them: a plague-type formula, not a unit that the seam 'cuts apart'. No ruled device - superscription, hallelu-Yah/hodu frame, doxology, acrostic, explicit speaker/addressee shift, refrain, Selah - stands on either side of any candidate cut.
